title: bisect — bisect_left, bisect_right, insort
signature: bisect_left(a, x) -> int | bisect_right(a, x) -> int | insort(a, x) -> None
summary: Binary search over an already-sorted sequence, and insertion that keeps it sorted.
description: `bisect` **assumes** the sequence is sorted and does not check. On unsorted input it returns a confident wrong answer rather than raising, which is worse than a crash.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: A sequence already in ascending order.

returns: An index, or None for insort.
real_world_usage: Banding a value into a range (grades, tax brackets, latency buckets), maintaining a sorted leaderboard, and finding the newest record before a timestamp.

common_mistakes.fix: It cannot detect this. Sort first, or maintain order as you insert.
The search is, the insert is not — the tail has to shift, so insort is O(n). Fine for read-heavy data, wrong for a write-heavy queue.
They differ only for values equal to an existing element: left returns the position before them, right after.

performance_notes: Search O(log n); insort O(n) because of the shift. If inserts dominate, use a heap, or the third-party sortedcontainers.
